posts.title: Seats in the house with 20% of the vote counted
posts.text: More numbers: this time seats in the house with 20% of the vote counted: National 42, Act 13, NZ First 12 = 67 seats Labour 35, Greens, 16, Te Pāti Māori 5 = 56 seats Opportunity 7 Currently, it is projected there would be 130 seats in the house. For an explanation on this, refer to our overhang post from earlier.

Some of the Labour party candidates are locked in neck and neck races, with tensions high for those at the Labour party event watching the candidates in Hutt South. With more than 20% of the vote counted, Labour’s Ginny Anderson has edged just ahead of the incumbent, National MP Chris Bishop, by just a handful of…
Couple of pics here from Jamie Tahana down at Backbenchers. Bound to be a few of you who know the inside of this place.

Another key feature of this election has been the possibility of an overhang - where a party wins more electorates than its share of the party vote. If that occurs, more seats will be added to parliament to make up the difference and could dictate which coalition can form a government. Te Pāti Māori (the Māori party)…

posts.title: National leading as 17% of vote counted
posts.text: Some more numbers, with 17% of the vote counted. National are on 30.5%, Labour 29%, the Greens 13%, Act 11.1%, NZ First 9.8%, Opportunity 5.4% and Te Pāti Māori 0.5%. We’re going to need to start discussing the prospect of overhang seats, as it is heading towards that scenario. We’ll have a post on this soon.

The race between Act leader David Seymour and National’s Paul Goldsmith in the Epsom seat is narrow – a matter of a few dozen votes. National supporters chanted “Goldsmith, Goldsmith”, when the results appeared on two giant screens, flanking the podium, at the Viaduct Events Centre.

Elsewhere in the Upper Hutt Cosmopolitan Club, punters were ordering crate bottles of local beer Tui and listening to a band kick up a rendition of Tennessee Whiskey. For Hutt locals, the Cossie Club is a social hub; karaoke on Thursdays, Bingo on Sundays, and a jug of lager for $14 during happy hour. While everyone…

Seven of the seats in New Zealand’s 120-seat parliament are Māori electorates. Voters of Māori descent can choose to vote on the Māori roll – allowing them to vote for these seats – or the general roll. More than half of Māori voters are on the Māori roll. They still get two votes; one for the electorate, and one for…

National party faithful are starting to trickle into its event at the cavernous Viaduct Event Centre on Auckland’s waterfront. The room is awash in blue light. People are grabbing drinks and milling around. The reaction is flicking between nervousness and excitement as the first numbers show the race is - as predicted…

As the first results of the night flashed up onto the big screen, Labour party volunteer Jasmine, 22, who works in the public service and didn’t want to use her last name, stopped talking mid-sentence. A hush fell over the room as the first poll results show the main parties neck and neck . “That’s close,” she said,…

Another update here with 8% of the vote counted. National on 31.2%, Labour 28.4%, the Greens 12.9%, Act 11.2%, NZ First 9.6%, Opportunity 5.7% and Te Pāti Māori 0.4%. On these numbers, we would have a right bloc coalition back in power. Long way to go.
